messages:
mara: Hey team — opened PR #7018 to add an AsyncIterator-based streaming API to the JS SDK. Can someone take a quick look? Hoping to get this merged EOD so we can ship the minor release.

kevin: URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/7018 — short summary: client.stream() now returns an async iterator that yields {chunk, done}. Also supports iterator.return() to cancel. Added unit + e2e tests. cc @jess for types

jess: I can review in ~30m. Quick Q: does this change tool-calling or function payloads at all?

mara: No change to the payloads themselves — this is a client-side streaming wrapper. Types bumped for the streaming event enum though.

ci-bot: CI started for branch mara/pr-7018 — running 3 checks (unit, lint, streaming-e2e)

ian: Heads up I saw a flaky streaming e2e last week that was related to backpressure. Does the iterator alter backpressure semantics?

mara: Good question — it preserves backpressure. The iterator awaits an internal queue drain before yielding. I added a slow-consumer test:

```js
for await (const {chunk} of client.stream(req)) {
  await sleep(200) // simulate slow consumer
  // process chunk
}
```

kevin: Note for browser adapter: we use ReadableStream under the hood. Make sure iterator.return() calls controller.close() or we'll leak.

mara: Addressed — browser adapter now calls controller.close() on return. Added unit to validate close is called.

jess: Found a TS mismatch in types.d.ts (line ~42) — AsyncIterator<T> generic isn't exported properly. I'll push a small type-only fix to the branch.

mara: Thanks — holding for that change before re-running CI.

ci-bot: Check failed: integration/streaming-e2e (timeout). Log excerpt: "stream timed out after 30s"

kevin: Likely the harness timeout. We bumped the harness yesterday; can you rebase on main?

mara: Great catch, rebased and force-pushed (commit 7c9f9b).

ci-bot: CI restarted for updated branch — 4 checks running.

jess: LGTM after my types fix. Left two tiny nits inline (non-blocking). :thumbsup:

ian: Verified locally that cancellation via iterator.return() properly closes underlying node stream and no memory growth observed.

mara: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll merge once CI is green and add a short release note to changelog.

kevin: Can you add a brief note to changelog/api.md explaining async iterator semantics + cancellation behavior? Helps platform teams.

mara: Yep, adding changelog entry now. Merging in ~10m if no objections. :shipit:

ci-bot: All checks passed — merging mara/pr-7018 (merged by automation)
